I’ve been farming these 19.1 mu in Quzhou for 15 years, since I was 21. I only finished primary school, but I can read a fertilizer bag and count money, and I learned everything from my mother-in-law and watching the neighbors. My family has eight people. My husband and his brother work in a factory in town and send money home, so we have some cash, but I still watch every yuan. I have 15 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, and 4.1 mu in cotton. The cotton is too much work to expand — picking it by hand takes forever — but the cotton money is cash in autumn when we need it.

For the wheat already in the field: Last autumn I rotary tilled and sowed improved wheat seed. I put one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer. This spring, I will top dress with half a bag of urea, about 20 jin per mu, when the wheat greens up. I irrigate four times total: the winter water is already done, then green-up, jointing, and grain filling. My well pump costs about 20 yuan of electricity each time per mu, but I don’t skip water. Three pesticide sprays total — herbicide before winter, then one for aphids and one for rust in spring. Last year I got 900 jin per mu. This year I hope for 480 kg per mu if the weather holds.

For maize on the same 15 mu: After wheat harvest in June, I plant hybrid maize seed using the no-till planter — there is no time to plough, and everyone here does no-till for summer maize. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, and top dress with 20 jin of urea per mu when the plants are knee-high. I irrigate two or three times, depending on rain. Two sprays: herbicide right after sowing, and one for corn borer. I expect 520 kg per mu.

For cotton on the 4.1 mu: I plant hybrid cotton in April. Rotary tillage first. Base fertilizer is one bag of compound fertilizer and some extra potassium fertilizer per mu — cotton needs potassium or the leaves turn yellow and the bolls drop. I top dress twice with urea, 10 jin each time. Three irrigations. Five pesticide sprays — I can’t skip any with cotton, the bollworm will destroy everything. Last year I got about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu. This year I expect 260 kg per mu.

I think about costs every day. A bag of compound fertilizer is about 150 yuan, urea is about 90 yuan. But I figured this out long ago: saving half a bag of urea saves 45 yuan, but if I lose even 50 jin of wheat, that is 65 yuan lost. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. So I would rather apply a bit too much than too little. I watch what my neighbors do. If Lao Wang uses the same amount and his crops look good, I do the same. Change is risky. I do what I did last year, and last year worked.
